# Tapstall

> Tapstall gives a shop one link: the customer taps it, picks, and pays the exact amount, and the order lands in a dashboard the shop owns.

Tapstall is a store-link and order rail for small retailers in Zimbabwe and South Africa, built for Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram sellers whose orders were previously scattered across chat.

Owner: Coldcode SI Labs, Harare, Zimbabwe.
Storefront: https://tapstall.whop.site
Markdown: https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/index.md
Facts (JSON): https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/facts.json

## What it does

- Menu first: Put the products and prices in once.
- Share the link: Post it where you already sell, including WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram.
- Exact amounts: The customer pays the exact amount, so the payment matches the order.
- Dashboard: Name, number, address, items and amount land in an order list the shop owns.
- Local payments: EcoCash, InnBucks, PayShap and ZIPIT are the expected rails.
- No order cap: No commission on orders and no hostage data.

## Questions

- [What is Tapstall?](https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/facts.json): Tapstall is a store link for small shops: a customer taps it, picks from the menu and pays the exact amount, and the order arrives in a dashboard the shop owns.
- [How much does Tapstall cost?](https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/facts.json): It is free for 60 days with no card. After that it is $7 a month or $60 a year, or R129 a month or R999 a year in South Africa.
- [Which payments does Tapstall work with?](https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/facts.json): The shops it is built for use EcoCash, InnBucks, PayShap and ZIPIT, alongside ordinary bank transfers.
- [Does Tapstall take a commission?](https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/facts.json): No. There is no order cap and no commission; the shop keeps its own order data and can export it to its own Google Sheet.
- [How long does it take to open a store?](https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/facts.json): About 90 seconds: put the menu in, share the link, and start taking orders from the chat apps the shop already sells in.
- [Does a customer need to install an app?](https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/facts.json): No. The store is a page behind a link, so it opens in whatever browser the customer already has.
- [Why not just use Shopify?](https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/facts.json): Shopify and the platforms built for Silicon Valley assume cards, couriers and a checkout flow that many shops in Zimbabwe and South Africa do not have. Tapstall is built around local payment rails and chat-based selling.
- [Who is Tapstall for?](https://tapstall-v2.tapstall.workers.dev/facts.json): Small retailers and social sellers in Zimbabwe and South Africa, especially those taking orders through WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram.
